method: commits_per_s is a gauge sampled by the harness on the writer's flush cadence (1314 samples over the run); hourly buckets are floor((ts - run_started_epoch)/3600) using run_started_epoch = min(ts) over all of metrics.jsonl (same convention as soak3's throughput-3.json). per_life_first_hour_avg averages samples in the first 3600s of each writer life (life boundaries = recoveries-4.jsonl t_death). hourly_edge_rows_avg is read directly off each compactions-4.jsonl row's own compact.edge_rows field (this run's compaction log carries epoch ts_start/ts_end directly, unlike soak3's host-uptime-only t_start/t_end, so no compactions_total counter reconciliation is needed here -- each row already carries its own life field and epoch ts_end for hour-bucketing).
note_on_manifest_vs_this_record: Manifest's own drift.throughput_first_hour_avg/last_hour_avg = 40.552 / 19.164 (ratio 0.473); this record's independently bucketed hour-0/hour-23 averages are 40.543 / 19.246 (ratio 0.475). The small (<1%) differences on both ends match the pattern soak3 documented and attributed to a different hour-0 clock origin (the harness's own internal start reference vs. this record's min(ts) over all of metrics.jsonl) -- not a computation error.
per_life_first_hour_avg_commits_per_s_no: life 0 starts at run_started_epoch, which is also hour-0 bucket zero, so life0 first-hour avg == this_record_first_hour_avg_commits_per_s exactly, by construction (not a coincidence).
